newsitem.title: USA: Gore urges Congress to pass disaster relief bill.
newsitem.headline: Gore urges Congress to pass disaster relief bill.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore and Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle Tuesday urged Senate Republicans to release disaster aid for flood-stricken states in a form President Clinton would sign into law.

Daschle, a Democrat whose own state of South Dakota was hard hit by spring floods, said the party will stop all Senate work until the relief issue is resolved. He and other Democrats in both chambers have vowed to hold an all-night vigil in support of disaster legislation.
Daschle and Gore appeared at a joint news conference in the Capitol.
"They (Republicans) want to tack on to it (the disaster aid) unrelated measures they cannot get passed unless they hold people hostage," Gore said.

Clinton vetoed the $8.6 billion spending bill Monday, citing his objection to three unrleatead provisions which he charged Republicans added for political purposes. Now, it is up to Republican leaders to decide whether to continue the confrontation or back down.
A spokeswoman for Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, Republican of Mississippi, said their next course of action had not yet been decided.
Daschle said Democratic senators will meet in his office for call-ins from the public and to speak with public officials.

House Minority Leader David Bonior, a Michigan Democrat, said House Democrats will also hold an all-night vigil outside the Senate chamber if the Senate is shut down. "We are going to drum this home to American people that there is no reason we can't have a clean diaster assistance bill," he said.
Daschle advocated passage of the $5.4 billion in disaster relief and other emergency funds as one bill with separate legislation and separate votes on the issues being advanced by Republicans.

One of these is designed to avert another government shutdown this fall by continuing fiscal 1998 spending at the 1997 level if regular money bills have not been enacted by the Oct 1 start of the 1998 fiscal year. Another would bar the use of sampling rather than head-by-head counts in the 2000 census.
